U.S. Navy tests camera system that spots sailors overboard
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
08:39:04 UTC
17:39:04 KST

- U.S. Navy engineers tested a thermal camera system on Aug. 14 that automatically detects sailors falling overboard, using a rescue dummy at Port Hueneme, California.
- The prototype uses commercial cruise ship software, and the team is now seeking new funding to test it aboard an active destroyer.
U.S. Navy engineers in California have tested a prototype camera system designed to spot a sailor falling overboard and alert the ship’s bridge automatically, throwing a 35-pound rescue dummy off the side of a decommissioned destroyer to see whether the cameras would catch it.
The test took place on Aug. 14 aboard the Self Defense Test Ship, which was docked at Port Hueneme, California, where a team from Naval Surface Warfare Center, Port Hueneme Division temporarily mounted the Man Overboard Detection System on the starboard side of the bow. Branch manager Eric King said the system worked flawlessly, although the bridge alarm it is meant to trigger was not part of the test.
King said he believes the system “bridges a gap by providing immediate, automated man-overboard alerts, enabling rapid-response search and rescue operations when seconds count.”
The prototype uses thermal cameras, which detect body heat and can work in darkness, mounted on metal pedestals that extend horizontally from the deck out over the water. For the test, the team installed two cameras in each of two pedestals placed about 61 meters (200 feet) apart and held them to the deck with powerful magnets and counterweights, while permanent versions would be welded in place.
“We needed two thermal cameras per pedestal because one of them captures the short-range blind spot view of the ship and the other camera captures the medium- to long-range view of the ship,” said systems engineer David Dozal, who leads the project.
Dozal said the software compares the overlapping views from opposing cameras to confirm that someone has gone over the side, which allows it to sound the bridge alarm in real time and give responders the exact location where the person entered the water. In a full installation, the cameras would ideally cover the entire perimeter of a U.S. Navy destroyer.
To simulate a fall, the team bought a 1.8-meter (6-foot) vinyl water rescue training dummy named OSCAR, after the international signal flag for “man overboard.” Dozal and mechatronics engineer Daniel Lopez dropped the dummy over the side several times on a rope, hauling it back aboard between throws, while computer engineers Jessica Diaz and Nayeli Mateo checked on a laptop inside the ship that the system had recorded each event correctly.
Much of the hardware and software came from the commercial market. The video analytics software was developed by a private company for the cruise ship industry, and the Navy team used part of its research funding to license it, while the same company built the pedestals to a design drawn up in-house at Port Hueneme. The four thermal cameras were bought off the shelf. The Navy did not name the company.
The cruise industry has a regulatory reason to build such tools: the Cruise Vessel Safety and Security Act, passed by Congress in 2010, requires passenger cruise ships to integrate technology that can capture images of passengers or detect those who have fallen overboard, to the extent such technology is available.
The Self Defense Test Ship itself is the former USS Paul F. Foster (DD 964), a Spruance-class destroyer decommissioned in 2003 and now used by the Port Hueneme division as a floating test platform, often operated by remote control, for ship self-defense weapons and sensors.
The project was funded through the Naval Innovative Science and Engineering program, which supports early-stage research at Navy warfare centers, but that money has now run out. King said the team needed the test results to prove the concept and has started talks with potential sponsors, including the possibility of folding the system into a larger program.
Dozal said the next step would ideally be a temporary installation aboard an active destroyer in San Diego, tested both in port and at sea, which would require a longer window, such as a maintenance period, to fit cameras around the whole ship and route cables safely.
“We also need to calculate the complete MOB installation cost to put it entirely around one Navy ship; we need those numbers to show to a funding source,” Dozal said.

New rules coming into force in Switzerland on November 1
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
08:38:32 UTC
17:38:32 KST

New rules coming into force in Switzerland on November 1
New rules are coming into force in Switzerland on November 1 that concern the transmission of air passenger data and Schengen personal data, as well as the modernisation of identity documents.
AVIATION SECURITY: Airlines will be required to submit detailed passenger data to a national authority, the Passenger Information Unit (PIU). The new regulation sets out the formats and timelines for this submission, with a view to combating terrorism and serious crime more effectively.
In future, passengers will be informed about the collection of their data before making a booking. This measure implements the Air Passenger Data Act passed by Parliament and aims to enhance security in the sector, while ensuring compliance with data protection regulations.
SCHENGEN: A new ordinance sets out in detail the national component of the Schengen Information System (SIS) and the tasks of the SIRENE Bureau in Switzerland, which is the national reference and coordination centre for the SIS at the Federal Office of Police (Fedpol). The text sets out the procedures by which the Swiss authorities manage and exchange personal data within the framework of international police cooperation.
+ Switzerland to collect data from non-Schengen visitors
The aim is to strengthen internal security and make border controls more effective by standardising data processing. This amendment serves to implement Switzerland’s international Schengen obligations and aims to ensure smooth cooperation with other Member States in the fight against crime.
IDENTITY DOCUMENTS: Switzerland is modernising its identity documents and amending the relevant ordinance. From November 1, the current “provisional passport” will be referred to as an “emergency passport”, which should provide greater clarity. Furthermore, in future, identity cards will be explicitly offered in two versions: with and without a chip.
The collection of biometric data – such as fingerprints – for passports and identity cards with chips is clarified, in line with international standards. The fees for the various types of documents have also been revised to take account of the administrative burden and technical innovations. The changes affect all Swiss citizens applying for a new passport or identity card.
AGRICULTURE: A new regime for the management of bovine viral diarrhoea (BVD) will come into force on Swiss livestock farms. The previous classification of holdings as “not subject to restrictions”, “subject to restrictions” and “subject to restrictions for individual animals” is being abolished. From now on, there will be only two categories: “BVD-free” or “not BVD-free”, the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO) has announced.
From November, BVD-free farms will be able to move animals without restrictions. For non-exempt holdings, however, restrictions will apply. The new regime marks the end of a two-year transitional phase towards the elimination of BVD in Switzerland. The FSVO is, in fact, pursuing the objective of eradicating the disease. To date, over 99% of cattle holdings are free from the virus.

France reports first human Shamonda virus case
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
08:36:24 UTC
17:36:24 KST

France reports first human case of livestock virus Shamonda after patient dies
- France reported its first human Shamonda virus case after a man in his 60s died, but officials said there is “no risk” to the general public.
- The patient likely caught the livestock virus from a midge in eastern France, where it spread among animals this spring and summer, according to the French government.
- WHO says it is in contact with France, while Shamonda has now been found in several European countries and can cut dairy farm milk output by up to 75%.
AI generated
PARIS – France on Oct 22 reported the first human case of the Shamonda virus usually found in livestock in a patient who later died, with the authorities adding there was no risk to the general population at this stage.
It is suspected that the victim was bitten by a midge carrying the virus in eastern France where it had circulated among animals this spring and summer, the French government said in a statement.
The UN’s World Health Organization (WHO) said it was in contact with the French authorities about the outbreak.
The patient died in early October and had been receiving treatment for a serious illness that made them more susceptible to infection than the general population, the Stockholm-based European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) said in a statement.
The victim was a man in 60s living in the Lyon area, local French newspaper Le Progres reported.
“Based on current information and knowledge of the transmission of closely related viruses, this is an isolated human case and it is unlikely to lead to wider spread at this time,” said the Geneva-based WHO, which coordinates responses to international public health issues and emergencies.
The French government also said no health risk to the general population had been identified.
Virus spreading in animals in Europe
Shamonda is transmitted by biting midges and most commonly found in cattle, though it has also been found in horses, alpaca, sheep and goats, according to the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH).
It is not classified as a disease under the EU Animal Health Law and not subject to official surveillance or control measures.
Identified in Nigeria in the mid-1960s, Shamonda was first confirmed in Europe in late July after genomic tests on sick cattle in southern Germany, Switzerland and eastern France.
France’s weekly animal health surveillance bulletin said the virus had also been detected in Austria, Belgium, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, and UK’s Jersey.
The virus has several effects on animals, with affected cattle showing diarrhoea, weakness, loss of appetite and, less often, fever, the French animal health authorities said.
A study of French nine dairy farms found milk output fell by up to 75%. REUTERS

Nordic force should turn north, committee suggests
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
09:30:20 BST
17:30:20 KST

The government should consider whether the Joint Expeditionary Force concentrates its finite resources on the High North instead of operating as often in the Baltic, and may need to build the British Army force in Estonia up to brigade strength to offset the change, according to a report by the Defence Committee.
The committee, chaired by Tan Dhesi, the Labour member for Slough, sets out that Britain permanently leads the ten-nation force, which brings together the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and the three Baltic and five Nordic countries, and that Britain has taken over command of NATO’s Joint Force Command Norfolk.
Dhesi said: “Our report calls for the government to reassess the JEF’s role and consider whether it should focus more on countering threats in the High North, particularly if the UK has to plan for uncertainty over US support for NATO. The UK’s presence in the Baltics, particularly in Estonia, may need to be bolstered to offset the effects of any greater JEF focus on the High North.”
The report recommends: “The government should consider whether the JEF focuses on the High North, concentrating finite resources on maximising its ability to operate more frequently in the harsh climate there while undertaking the demanding anti-submarine mission, rather than operating as often in the Baltic as previously.”
On Estonia it states: “To offset this greater focus on the High North the UK may need to reassure Baltic members of the JEF by reinforcing its commitment there in other ways; for example, by building up the current British Army force in Estonia to brigade-size, to match what Germany is already doing in Lithuania.”
A separate recommendation asks the government, within a year of assuming leadership of Joint Force Command Norfolk, to reassess the added value the force brings to European security, stating that either it provides distinct value alongside NATO and should be strengthened and aligned more closely with it, or it does not and Britain should focus its finite resources on NATO.
The committee sets out that the force was established in 2014 for rapid, scalable operations with northern European allies, and that its principal value lies below the Article 5 threshold where it can respond to hybrid threats, protect undersea infrastructure and act more quickly than NATO’s full consensus-based machinery. During an overseas committee visit, one commentator referred to the force as “a jack of all trades and therefore master of no military tasks.”
The report records that the force overlaps with NATO tasks and has not always proved faster than NATO in practice, that it lacks some major NATO powers including Canada, and that it neither specialises in the shallow waters of the Baltic nor in anti-submarine operations in the harshness of the High North.
Canada applied to join the force in September 2026, and the committee notes that it could add valuable experience and capabilities given its long experience of operating in harsh regional conditions and its membership of the Five Eyes intelligence group, but that adding the North American Arctic to the European High North would significantly increase the force’s area of responsibility.
With Sweden and Finland having joined NATO, the committee observes that eight of the nine countries around the Baltic Sea are now members of the alliance and offer significant capabilities of their own in that region.
The Ministry of Defence told the committee that “[o]nce we transition into crisis, the chances are that the JEF will, in some way, fold into the regional plan north-west anyway. There is not a competition between the two; they are entirely complementary and one supports the other.”

Hong Kong’s surging exports amid recent global trade shifts and tariff measures are reason to celebrate. However, they have not reversed the decline in the city’s port’s container throughput, which hit 12.99 million 20-foot equivalent units in 2025, down 5.1 per cent year on year.

As Hong Kong pivots towards maritime services, there are fundamental questions about the strategic purpose of the city’s physical port in a value-driven era. How should the port evolve so physical cargo flows power Hong Kong’s high-value service ecosystem instead of lagging behind?

Ukraine faces a new Russian cruise missile called Filin
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
08:29:56 UTC
17:29:56 KST

- Ukrainian military intelligence published a 3D model and component breakdown of Russia’s Filin cruise missile, first used against Ukraine in late summer 2026.
- The ground-launched missile has a claimed range of up to 1,200 km and contains 35 American and 22 Chinese components.
Ukraine’s military intelligence agency has published a detailed breakdown of Filin, a new Russian ground-launched cruise missile that Moscow began firing at Ukraine in late summer 2026. According to the agency, the missile combines a composite airframe and a Russian jet engine with onboard electronics built largely from American and Chinese parts.
The Main Intelligence Directorate of Ukraine’s Defense Ministry, known as HUR, released an interactive 3D model of the missile, its main assemblies and a catalog of its electronic components on the agency’s War & Sanctions portal. The agency did not say how many Filin missiles Russia has launched, which targets they hit or how investigators obtained the parts they examined.
Filin, Russian for “eagle owl,” is made by AO NPO Molniya, a company within Russia’s state-owned Tactical Missiles Corporation. HUR described the missile as the latest product of a Russian effort to build relatively cheap jet-powered strike weapons that launch from the ground instead of from aircraft or warships.
The missile is 3.5 meters (11.5 feet) long and has a wingspan of 3 meters (9.8 feet), with a maximum launch weight of 210 kg (463 pounds). Its fuselage is made of carbon fiber and fiberglass composites, and some of its parts are produced by 3D printing, an approach that can cut manufacturing time and cost compared with traditional machined components.
Russia claims Filin can reach a top speed of 800 km/h (497 mph) and fly up to 1,200 km (746 miles), although HUR’s specification sheet gives the range as 600 to 1,200 km (373 to 746 miles), which suggests the figure depends on the configuration. The missile can fly at very low altitude, where ground-based radar has a harder time detecting incoming threats, or climb as high as 6 km (19,700 feet).
Filin comes in versions with either a 50 kg (110-pound) or a 100 kg (220-pound) warhead, and HUR lists three warhead types: high-explosive fragmentation, penetrating and thermobaric. A thermobaric warhead first disperses an explosive cloud and then ignites it, producing a longer and more powerful blast wave than a conventional charge of similar weight.
The missile is fired from a ground launcher with the help of a solid-fuel booster, which pushes it up to flying speed before its small jet engine takes over for the cruise to the target.
HUR’s investigation also links Filin closely to Russia’s long-range attack drone program. The missile’s onboard equipment is produced by OOO PLAZ, which also makes equipment for the Garpiya, or “Harpy,” drone, a modification of the Geran-2 built in several series by the Izhevsk Electromechanical Plant Kupol. The Geran-2 itself is Russia’s version of the Iranian-designed Shahed-136, and HUR said electronic units from Filin and Garpiya share a similar layout and similar markings.
For guidance, Filin relies on a Chinese-made inertial navigation system, which tracks the missile’s position using onboard motion sensors without any outside signal. It works alongside a 16-channel Kometa satellite navigation module, a jam-resistant receiver made by Russia’s VNIIR-Progress that has repeatedly turned up in Russian drones and guided bombs recovered in Ukraine.
HUR said Filin’s electronics resemble those found in other Russian missiles and drones, but with a larger share of Chinese parts and with the same design solutions reused across different units and circuit boards. Investigators counted 35 American components and 22 Chinese ones in the missile’s onboard equipment.
The identified suppliers include Texas Instruments, Analog Devices, NXP Semiconductors and STMicroelectronics, along with Chinese firms such as WinChipHead and Mornsun. Production markings on some parts date from 2021 and 2022, including an Ethernet switch chip made in May 2022, three months after Russia launched its full-scale invasion.
Filin’s engine, by contrast, is Russian: an R500 turbojet built by OOO Reynolds. HUR had previously identified the same engine in Russia’s S-71K Kover air-launched cruise missile and in the S-71M Monokhrom.

Most of the drones were intercepted by air defences at long range, while 163 were destroyed on approach to Moscow, Sobyanin added.
In a separate statement, the Russian defence ministry said its forces had carried out a large-scale overnight strike using precision-guided ground-launched weapons and unmanned aerial vehicles.
According to the ministry, the strikes targeted Ukrainian military-industrial enterprises involved in the production and storage of cruise missiles and medium- and long-range drones, as well as transport infrastructure in Kiev and port infrastructure in the Odessa region.
The ministry also said vessels used in the interests of the Ukrainian armed forces had been targeted.
The claims by both sides could not been independently verified.

Swiss government opposes initiative to restrict fireworks
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
08:17:31 UTC
17:17:31 KST

Swiss government opposes initiative to restrict fireworks
The federal government recommends rejecting the fireworks initiative that will be voted on by the Swiss people on November 29. It argues that the cantons and municipalities already have the legal basis to restrict fireworks.
The popular initiative referred to as the Fireworks Restriction Initiative calls for a ban on fireworks that produce noise. Accordingly, loud fireworks, such as firecrackers and bangers, would no longer be permitted to be sold to private individuals. Furthermore, private individuals would no longer be permitted to set off loud fireworks.
The Federal Council is aware, as stated in its message to parliament, that loud fireworks are perceived as a nuisance by some members of the public and can trigger severe reactions in animals. However, the noise and the particulate matter emissions from fireworks – also cited by the initiative committee – are temporary and comparatively low.
More
The Federal Council goes on to say that many people in the country associate very positive emotions with setting off fireworks. In its view, nationwide restrictions on the sale and use of fireworks are therefore unnecessary and disproportionate.

Ukraine Receives Finnish Variant of Crotale Air Defense System to Counter Russian Drones and Missiles
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
08:16:24 UTC
17:16:24 KST

Ukraine’s 1039th Anti-Aircraft Missile Regiment, named after General Mykola Kapustianskyi, has received Finnish ItO 90M air defense systems.
The delivery was revealed in a video showing the systems in operation, published on the regiment’s Facebook account.
The ItO 90M is Finland’s version of the French Crotale NG short-range air defense system, developed by Thales.
The main difference in the Finnish version is its use of the Sisu XA-181 6×6 armored personnel carrier chassis instead of a French-made vehicle.
The story of this deal began in 1988, when Finland signed an agreement with France to purchase 21 Crotale NG air defense systems for its armed forces.
The Finnish systems underwent a major upgrade in the 2000s, receiving modern thermal imaging systems, upgraded daylight cameras, and improved fire-control systems. These upgrades are reflected in the designation ‘M,’ which stands for Modernisoitu (modernized).
The history of the Crotale NG system dates back to the late 1980s, when French developers created a new air defense system designed to engage cruise missiles, unmanned aerial vehicles, and low-flying aircraft.
The standard Crotale NG system integrates a radar detection system, electro-optical tracking equipment, and an eight-missile launcher on a single turret.
In terms of its technical specifications, the ItO 90M can detect aerial targets at ranges of up to 20 km.
Its primary interceptor is the high-speed VT-1 missile, which reaches speeds of up to Mach 3.5 (approximately 1,200 m/s) and has an engagement range of up to 11 km and an engagement altitude of up to 6 km.
The system has a reaction time of just five seconds from target detection to missile launch, enabling it to effectively intercept high-speed aerial targets.
As previously reported, Ukrainian air defense forces used a combination of a Kub surface-to-air missile system launcher and a Buk self-propelled firing unit to shoot down Russian jet-powered drones.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Ministry of Education said Thursday that Shih Hsin University must improve consultation with students after investigators identified serious failures in its introduction of campus reforms, CNA reported.
The ministry sent a team to investigate complaints and meet with university officials and students. Department of Higher Education Director-General Liao Kao-hsien (廖高賢) said the university had failed to properly consult students before introducing its new administrative structure.
CommonWealth Magazine reported that the university merged individual department offices into shared college-level offices. Students opposed the changes, saying the loss of department staff had made administrative services harder to access.
Students also criticized the university for converting part of its library into recreational spaces with karaoke rooms and gaming equipment. They questioned why the school was investing in entertainment facilities while classrooms and teaching resources needed improvement.
The university defended the restructuring, saying it would clarify administrative responsibilities and improve services. It said the library renovations aimed to make better use of existing space and serve a wider range of student needs, per CTEE.
A student group launched a protest campaign on Oct. 8, calling for greater transparency in university spending. During the university’s 70th anniversary celebration at Taipei Arena on Oct. 14, security guards blocked protesters from entering, and a union member was pushed to the ground during the confrontation, per CTS News.
The university later said it respected students’ right to express their views but insisted that protesters follow event rules. It said security measures were necessary to protect attendees and maintain order, per TVBS News.
Following its investigation, the ministry instructed the university to respond directly to student concerns. Liao said the school might need to suspend the new administrative structure if it was found to harm students’ rights.
Universities must protect education quality and student rights when introducing reforms, Education Minister Cheng Ying-yao (鄭英耀) said. He warned that the ministry could cut government subsidies or reduce enrollment quotas if the university failed to make improvements within a specified period, per UDN.
DPP Legislator Chen Hsiu-pao (陳秀寶) said universities had the right to manage their own affairs but must not ignore students’ concerns. She urged the ministry to establish clearer measures to ensure improvements, per Knews.

Chen questioned why administrative neutrality rules should prevent audience members from expressing their political views.

Our Theatre posted a notice discouraging audiences from placing political material on the message board. Tsai clarified that he called the troupe after theater administrators expressed concern about political messages and performers objected to removing audience contributions, per UDN. He stressed that the call came after Our Theatre sought clarification on the matter.
Explaining the restrictions, Tsai said Wellspring Theater's code of conduct prohibits uses related to political activities. He warned that allowing political messages could cause the feedback area to stray from discussions about the art.
Tsai added that the city government would not object if the message board were outside the theater. He argued that Culture Minister Li Yuan (李遠) would take similar measures if a comparable situation arose at the National Theater and Concert Hall.
Tsai emphasized that the Taipei City Government had not asked Our Theatre to remain politically neutral but had urged the troupe to respect the theater’s rules, per NOWNews. He also called on Shen to familiarize himself with political neutrality requirements for performance spaces administered by the city government.
In a press release, Our Theatre producer Chang Hsin-i (張歆宜) said Tsai had advised removing the campaign stickers to prevent the troupe from becoming embroiled in political disputes over audience members’ views, per Liberty Times. She added that Tsai supported using the notice to remind audiences of the rules governing the message board.
Chang later said that while audience members were free to express their views, the troupe would remove politically related messages from the board every night.

Taiwan conducts observation flight to improve Typhoon Champi forecasts
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
08:12:38 UTC
17:12:38 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Central Weather Administration said Thursday that it had completed an observation flight to gather data on Typhoon Champi earlier that morning, according to a press release.
The CWA partnered with National Taiwan University and the Aerospace Industrial Development Corporation for the mission. An Astra jet departed Taichung’s Ching Chuan Kang Airport at 5 a.m. for a flight lasting about five hours.
The aircraft flew at an altitude of about 13,000 meters and deployed weather instruments called dropsondes around the typhoon and along its potential path. The instruments collected atmospheric temperature, pressure, humidity, wind direction, and wind speed data as they descended toward the sea.
The data were transmitted by satellite to the CWA to help forecasters analyze Champi’s structure and development. They were also fed into numerical forecasting models to improve predictions.
The CWA said observations over the ocean were relatively sparse, while forecasting models differed in their projections of Champi’s path and circulation. The flight gathered data from key areas to help address those gaps.
Taiwan has completed 92 observation flights under the program since 2003, improving typhoon monitoring and forecast accuracy, the CWA said. It also shared the Champi observations with weather agencies worldwide.

Taiwan urges PHP updates after critical flaws discovered
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
08:12:33 UTC
17:12:33 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Administration for Cyber Security (ACS) on Thursday urged government agencies, schools, and businesses to update PHP promptly after two critical vulnerabilities were found that could allow attackers to remotely execute malicious code.
PHP (Personal Home Page) is a programming language widely used to build websites, content management systems, and administrative interfaces. ACS urged organizations to check their PHP versions and install updates as soon as possible.
The two flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each received a severity score of 9.2 out of 10 under version 4.0 of the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, per CNA. Patches were released at 10 p.m. Taiwan time Wednesday, ACS said.
ACS Director-General Tsai Fu-lung (蔡福隆) said an inventory found approximately 28,000 publicly accessible websites use PHP, including about 200 government websites, per CNA. However, he said not all versions of PHP are affected, so the number of affected websites is expected to be lower.
PHP underpins platforms including WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento, and may also be used in software that does not explicitly identify itself as PHP-based, the agency said. Organizations should inventory PHP-based systems and related packages, verify their versions, and apply patches according to instructions.
After updating, organizations should review system logs for unusual access and check the security of accounts and credentials if suspicious activity is found. The agency said it would continue monitoring vulnerabilities to help public and private organizations reduce risks.

One of the highlights of the initiative is building ecological culture from an early age. 295 environmental preschool organizations were set up as part of the Zhasyl balabaksha project (Green kindergarten), and over 158,000 ecological classes were taught at schools.
Taza Qazaqstan is not just an environmental campaign but also a common striving for cleanliness, commitment, and ecological culture, the Ecology Ministry said in a statement.

Defence Readiness Bill due before end of this Parliament
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
09:00:28 BST
17:00:28 KST

Legislation giving the government the powers it needs to respond effectively during escalation towards war is being developed and will be brought forward before the end of this Parliament, to be introduced when parliamentary time allows, according to an answer given in Parliament.
Damien Egan, the Labour member for Bristol North East, asked whether the Secretary of State plans to introduce new legislation on defence readiness and national resilience during the current legislative session.
Luke Pollard, the Minister of State for Defence, said: “The Government has accepted the 2025 Strategic Defence Review recommendation to introduce a Defence Readiness Bill to ensure the Government has the powers it needs to respond effectively during escalation towards war. Prospective legislation is being developed to be brought forward before the end of this Parliament and will be introduced when parliamentary time allows.”
The Strategic Defence Review published in June 2025 recommended the bill as part of its whole-of-society approach, and the powers under discussion cover the things a government would need to do quickly in a crisis: directing industrial production, requisitioning assets, mobilising reserves at scale and moving forces and materiel across the country without the peacetime consents that normally apply. Much of the existing statutory framework dates from the Cold War or earlier.
The timetable runs to the end of this Parliament, which gives the department until the next general election. This publication reported in the summer that the government was targeting the later part of the Parliament for the readiness bill, and today’s answer holds to that position while confirming that drafting work is under way.
Ministers confirmed in separate answers the same day that government messaging on defence and security will continue to build ahead of Exercise ALBISTON SHADOW, a major United Kingdom home defence exercise, and NATO’s Crisis Management Exercise in spring 2027, with the Security Minister and the Minister for the Armed Forces chairing chief executive threat briefings for critical national infrastructure and industry leaders.
A bill of this kind would attract scrutiny from across the House on the balance between emergency powers and ordinary liberties, which is the argument that slowed similar legislation in the past, and parliamentary time grows scarce in the back half of a Parliament. The department has roughly half of this one left to work with.

Court reduces Meta’s fine from $219 billion to $25 billion

Court reduces Meta’s fine from $219 billion to $25 billion
A New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for misleading Facebook users. The company deceived them about personal data protection, Qazinform News Agency reports.
Judge Francis Mathew issued the ruling on October 21. Jurors found nearly 43.9 million willful violations of the state’s Unfair Practices Act.
The case concerned Facebook’s public statements from May 2010 through August 2021. The company promised users control over their personal information. However, the court found that its privacy settings often failed to provide that control.
Specifically, limiting a post’s audience did not determine what information third-party developers could access. The company knew users did not understand the settings and exploited that confusion.
“Facebook was aware that its users did not understand its privacy settings and took advantage of that to a grossly unfair degree,” the ruling stated.
Statements found unlawful included those by Mark Zuckerberg and former Chief Operating Officer Sheryl Sandberg. The court described them as part of a coordinated strategy to mislead the public.
The company continued making promises despite internal warnings that it could not fulfill them. These concerned data access, efforts to combat misinformation, and enforcement of platform rules.
The court calculated the penalty using the maximum rate of $5,000 per violation. The total exceeded $219 billion, but the court reduced it to $25 billion. The penalty will accrue interest at 15% annually until paid in full.
The court also noted that previous penalties had failed to stop the violations. These included a $5 billion settlement with the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.
Earlier, Qazinform News Agency reported that Meta unveiled its Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full artificial intelligence models.

Batumi Sea Port boosts cargo throughput by 13% in first nine months of 2026
Batumi Sea Port handled 6.25 million tons of cargo from January to September 2026, marking a 13 percent increase year on year, with growth recorded across all major cargo categories. The port is operated by a subsidiary of Kazakhstan’s oil pipeline company KazTransOil, Qazinform News Agency reports.
According to the company’s press service, Batumi Sea Port in Georgia reported an increase in cargo throughput during the first nine months of 2026, supported by higher volumes of dry bulk, containerized, ferry and liquid bulk cargo.
Containerized cargo accounted for the largest share of total throughput, reaching 2.984 million tons, up 17 percent compared with the same period in 2025.
Dry bulk cargo throughput totaled 1.434 million tons, representing a 7 percent on-year increase, while liquid bulk cargo volumes rose by 5 percent to 1.429 million tons.
Ferry cargo recorded the strongest growth among the main categories, increasing by 54 percent to 402,000 tons during the reporting period. The increase was supported, among other factors, by the introduction of an additional weekly ferry service on the Constanța-Batumi route.
The positive performance across all major cargo categories contributed to the port’s overall throughput growth of 13% in January-September 2026.

Study finds AI won't solve skills shortage in Switzerland
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
07:56:34 UTC
16:56:34 KST

Study finds AI won’t solve skills shortage in Switzerland
Artificial intelligence is transforming the Swiss labour market, but it is unlikely to resolve the skills shortage caused by demographic trends. Human workers remain in demand in sectors such as care, the skilled trades and transport, as a study by Deloitte Switzerland shows.
According to the study published on Thursday, AI could make tasks in the areas of documentation, planning, administration and information retrieval easier. In software and marketing roles, for example, job losses cannot be ruled out.
However, current AI systems are unlikely, for the foreseeable future, to be able to care for the elderly or the sick, teach children or carry out manual labour. The labour shortage is therefore likely to persist – and may even worsen – in people-oriented, service-oriented and practice-oriented professions, despite the advent of AI.
+ How artificial intelligence is shaping the Swiss job market
This points to a potential divide: “In Switzerland, many vacancies in occupations where AI can hardly take over the core tasks are likely to remain unfilled, while in other, often knowledge-intensive office-based roles, AI will automate tasks and create new requirements,” say the study’s authors.
Focus on vocational training and career changes
According to the study, businesses, educational institutions and policymakers should therefore strengthen vocational training and, in professions such as care, hospitality, logistics and the skilled trades, both facilitate career changes and create attractive career paths. Furthermore, AI is expected to relieve employees in occupations facing skills shortages of repetitive tasks, while in office and knowledge-based occupations, further training and new job profiles will be required.
For the study, Deloitte combined demographic and occupational data from Switzerland with international data on the use and potential applications of AI. A total of 279 occupations were examined.

====================================================================================================

Spring flood water levels in northern rivers to be forecasted using AI
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
07:47:36 UTC
16:47:36 KST

ST. PETERSBURG, October 22. /TASS/. The highest water levels in the northern rivers during the spring flood will be forecasted using artificial intelligence. The long-term forecasting method was developed by scientists of the Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute (AARI, St. Petersburg), the institution's press service said.
"Traditional methods of forecasting spring floods rely on snow reserves data. However, in the Arctic regions, in early March, this information remains insufficient for early forecasts: the snow accumulation still continues there. The sparse observation network and snow transport by snowstorms add to the difficulties, and due to this, individual measurements' results cannot always reflect correctly the situation in the entire area. When developing new methods of forecasting spring water rise levels, the scientists additionally took into account effects of autumn moisture and winter soil freezing," the press service said.
What additionally affects the water levels in spring is the autumn weather, including how intensive rains are and at what rate marshes are freezing up.
"In the tundra, rainy autumn and swamps, overflowing with moisture, turn the earth's surface layer into a solid ice shield during winter freezing. Further on, in spring, during the snowmelt period, the frozen soil absorbs meltwater much worse, and thus the water enters river channels in bigger amounts. It is this feature that contributes to the formation of high floods in Russia's northern regions. In case of dry autumns, the soil can absorb more meltwater, which cuts the risk of a sharp rise in river levels," the press service explained.
According to institute's representatives, in the control area - on rivers of the Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Region - the accuracy of forecasts that use the new methods was more than 80%, which is almost twice higher than regular climate forecasts have.
Practical application
The research, aimed at developing long-term hydrometeorology forecast methods for rivers and seas of the Russian Arctic in the changing climate, was conducted by AARI specialists for further use at the Ob-Irtysh Department of the Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring.
The scientists have created a system of 120 physical features to build digital models for rivers of the Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Region. The system includes rates of groundwater supply depletion, changes in water levels, accumulation and redistribution of water reserves, as well as dynamics of hydrological processes.
The algorithms were adjusted taking into account specifics of every basin, including for the Nadym, the Pur, the Taz, and the Pyaku-Pur Rivers.
"Basins of the Nadym, the Pur and the Taz Rivers are of strategic importance for the Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Region's oil and gas industry. Here are big deposits, compressor stations, and main gas pipelines, therefore extreme floods may pose a serious threat to the region's industrial and transport infrastructures. An important feature of northern rivers is that they flow mainly from south to north. Thus, in spring, meltwater rushes to the estuaries, where the ice cover may still remain thick and durable. This creates conditions for the formation of ice jams that obstruct the water flow and lead to a sharp increase in its level," senior researcher at AARI's Department of Hydrology of Estuaries and Water Resources Nadezhda Volkova said.
According to her, the developed methods will be used to assess well in advance risks of dangerous flood developments to plan preventive measures.

Committee questions whether attack submarines put to sea
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
08:30:19 BST
16:30:19 KST

Evidence of low availability among destroyers, frigates and attack submarines raises serious questions about whether Britain can meet its High North commitments before new capabilities enter service, according to a report by the Defence Committee.
The committee, chaired by Tan Dhesi, the Labour member for Slough, records reporting that all five of the Astute class nuclear attack submarines then in service had recently been tied up in dockyards at the same time, with none deployed.
Dhesi said: “The UK needs to be willing to address a hard truth: it does not currently have all the capabilities to operate successfully in the High North. Russian submarine and sabotage forces in the High North pose direct risks to the North Atlantic and the UK, including the nuclear deterrent. Despite this, the Ministry of Defence has accepted a serious anti-submarine warfare gap. Publicly available evidence of low availability among destroyers, frigates and attack submarines calls into question whether the UK can meet its commitments in the High North.”
Professor David Blagden of the University of Exeter told the committee: “[i]t was reported in the media quite recently that a French SSN [attack submarine] had been seen in Faslane around the time that one of [our] SSBNs sailed on its patrol… [i]s this the French now doing ‘delousing’ for a UK nuclear deterrent submarine going on patrol? Is that great alliance solidarity or is it, ‘Oh my god, we can’t get one of our own SSNs to sea to do one of the highest missions?'”
Delousing is the activity in which an attack submarine sanitises the waters around a ballistic missile submarine to ensure it is not being tracked or tailed by an adversary as it leaves on or returns from a deterrent patrol.
The Rt Hon the Lord Case, chair of Team Barrow, told the committee in November 2025 that the government is saying to the defence industry “[p]lease, how quickly can you build our nuclear submarines for us? We are having to make up for decades of neglect.”
Retired Rear Admiral Philip Mathias, a former Director of Nuclear Policy at the Ministry of Defence, said in December 2025 that one consequence of a lack of investment in the submarine fleet was that the duration of patrols for Vanguard class crews, which were seventy days during the Cold War, were now more than two hundred days, and that there was a shockingly low availability of submarines to counter the Russian threat in the High North.
The committee’s conclusion states: “The Royal Marines’ Arctic expertise is a significant national strength, but it cannot compensate for shortfalls in the naval platforms needed to deploy, protect and sustain operations in the region. The UK’s ability to deter and respond to threats in the High North depends not only on future programmes, but also on the readiness of the Royal Navy’s existing ships, submarines and specialist forces. Russian submarine and seabed warfare capabilities based in the High North pose direct risks to the North Atlantic, UK waters and the nuclear deterrent. Evidence of low availability among destroyers, frigates and attack submarines therefore raises serious questions about whether the UK can meet its High North commitments before new capabilities enter service.”
The committee asks the government to provide a plan setting out how the department will improve the availability of the Royal Navy’s frigates, destroyers and attack submarines before 2030, noting that the update might be presented at a classified level but that it expects a version to be made publicly available.
Ministers have consistently declined to disclose submarine availability, and Luke Pollard MP told Parliament this week that it is British policy not to disclose the operational availability or deployment details of submarines, as doing so would be likely to prejudice the capability, effectiveness or security of the armed forces.

====================================================================================================

Feature: Wuhan Open spurs spending boom
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
15:25:31 CST
16:25:31 KST

by sportswriters Yue Wenwan and Yu Xi
WUHAN, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- For years, when Vietnamese businessman Dang Phu visited China in autumn, his destination was always the Canton Fair. This year, he and two colleagues arrived three days earlier than usual to watch some of the world's best women's tennis players in action.
"We wanted to see top players compete in person and experience the atmosphere," Dang said.
The Wuhan Open, the season's final WTA 1000 event, was held at the Optics Valley International Tennis Center from Oct. 10 to 18, drawing 105 players from 38 countries and regions.
In previous years, the tournament coincided with "Golden Week," the weeklong Chinese National Day holiday in early October that drives a surge in travel and shopping across China. This year, the event fell outside the holiday period, yet it drew a record 202,700 spectator visits, 52,700 more than last year.
An assessment by organizers put the tournament's overall economic benefits at about 890 million yuan (around 133 million U.S. dollars), up 26.24 percent from a year earlier.
Dang's detour reflects how professional sports are creating new reasons for people to travel and new opportunities for cities to attract consumers beyond traditional holiday peaks.
TENNIS FUELS TOURISM
Much of the tournament's appeal comes from a growing community of fans who follow the sport beyond their hometowns. According to organizers, visitors from outside Wuhan accounted for 48 percent of this year's spectators.
At the Wuhan Open, spectators could be seen carrying rackets and wearing tennis outfits, with some arriving with plans to play as well as watch.
Cui Guorong, a tennis enthusiast from Chengdu in southwest China, bought tickets for three days with her doubles partner. Afterward, they planned to travel to nearby Xianning for an amateur event organized by the International Tennis Federation.
Cui has built her travels around tennis in recent years, watching tournaments in London and Paris, as well as in cities across China, including Beijing, Shanghai, Huangshan and Wenzhou.
"I came here both to watch matches and to play," Cui said, who practiced tennis in the morning and watched professional players in the afternoon and evening sessions.
"At my age, there are some techniques I can't master myself, but watching these players still gives me inspiration, and is a pleasure in itself," she added.
For fans like Cui, the Wuhan Open is more than a ticketed event. It becomes the centerpiece of a trip, with practice sessions and amateur competitions extending their stays and spending in the region.
FROM MATCH TICKETS TO SHOPPING BAGS
Local authorities and businesses have been working to harness the enthusiasm and spread its economic benefits beyond the stadium.
Hubei Province issued 20 million yuan in consumer vouchers, while Wuhan offered another 10 million yuan in sports vouchers. Other initiatives included tennis-themed travel itineraries, discounts for visitors presenting match tickets and live screenings in shopping districts.
Outside the tennis center, a fan festival covering about 10,000 square meters brought together more than 100 stalls selling sports equipment, local specialties, food, drinks and other goods.
At a stand for Tim Hortons, the Canadian coffee chain, drinks passed through the service window one after another as customers queued in long lines.
"The tournament offered an opportunity to boost both sales and brand recognition," said Wang Xiuping, the brand's regional operations manager for Hubei and neighboring Hunan province, adding that the successful try in Wuhan encouraged the company to participate in more sporting events in China.
At a temporary Wilson store, customers crowded around displays of tennis rackets, comparing models and seeking advice. Some out-of-town visitors arranged to have their purchases shipped home.
Sales at the store rose 10 percent from the same period last year, said Ye Xiufeng, who managed the stall.
The tournament's reach also extended into the evenings. Large screens in major shopping centers broadcast matches alongside amateur tennis challenges and other activities. Organizers said the "second-screen venues" attracted 12 million visits and generated nearly 300 million yuan in consumer spending during the event.
BUILDING A MARKET BEYOND NINE DAYS
The longer-term question is whether a major tournament can do more than create a temporary spending surge. An amateur team competition held alongside the Wuhan Open at the same tennis center offered one answer.
As Latvia's Jelena Ostapenko faced a British opponent in the tournament's semifinals, three outdoor courts nearby hosted the finals of the Wuhan Open city club circuit, an amateur team competition that has been running for more than a decade.
The circuit held qualifying events in seven cities this year, drawing more than 2,100 players from about 150 clubs across China.
Liu Fen, president of Wuhan's Chongren Tennis Club, whose team finished second, said playing on the same grounds as world-class athletes brought a special sense of pride.
"As amateur players, sharing the same grounds with the world's top players fills us with a tremendous sense of fulfillment and pride," Liu said.
She has witnessed how the sport has grown in Wuhan over more than a decade. Her club started with just one court and a dozen members.
"After Li Na won her Grand Slam title, more and more people started playing tennis. After Zheng Qinwen won Olympic gold in 2024, the number of players grew many times over, and courts began springing up everywhere," Liu said.
The club now has 365 members, more than 100 of whom gathered at the tournament venue each day during the Wuhan Open.
"For local tennis amateurs, Wuhan Open is an annual celebration. The exciting matches and warm atmosphere make us want to come every day. We often start watching at 11 a.m. and stay until 11 p.m.," Liu said.
The enthusiasm is already carrying into next year. After the club circuit's finals, members began preparing for the next edition.
"Everyone is even more motivated after this year's finals. We hope to have more teams reach the finals next year and show the world what amateur players like us can do," Liu said. ■

ROTTERDAM, the Netherlands, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- With only half an hour remaining before the women's team final at the Artistic Gymnastics World Championships, China was forced to make a crucial change to its lineup.
Suffering from a foot injury, Zhang Yihan had to withdraw from all her routines. World champion Zhang Qingying stepped in at the last minute, putting the team's contingency planning to the test before the first Chinese gymnast had even taken to the floor on Wednesday.
With all 12 routines completed cleanly across four apparatus, China claimed its first women's team gold in 20 years at the World Championships with 165.764 points, edging the United States by 0.233 and ending the Americans' run of seven consecutive titles. Both teams and bronze medalist Japan qualified for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
"We have no chance to make any mistake. So everyone must fight for every 0.1 point," said Chang Cheng, head of the Chinese delegation.
Zhang Yihan had originally been scheduled to perform a vault with a difficulty score of 5.2, as she did in qualification. Following the last-minute substitution, China opted for two vaults each rated at 5.0 and one at 4.4, seeking to maximize its score with the revised lineup.
"I just made a quick warm-up. Once the event got underway and everyone started jumping, I didn't even have time to feel nervous," Zhang Qingying said, describing how she stepped up at the last minute.
She scored 13.233 on vault and went on to compete on the uneven bars, balance beam and floor exercise, becoming the only Chinese gymnast that evening to compete on all four apparatus.
In the team final, three gymnasts compete on each apparatus and all three scores count toward the total. Unlike in qualification, there is no room to discard the lowest score. From domestic training through their arrival in Rotterdam, the team had prepared for scenarios in which the final routine by the final gymnast could determine the overall result.
In the third rotation on balance beam, China scored a combined 43.366 points, taking a 2.200-point lead over the United States into the final rotation. However, the last apparatus, floor exercise, was a strong event for the American team.
In the end, China held on to win by 0.233 points.
"We nailed all 12 routines," said Chang. "That's what matters."
From the Asian Championships to the Asian Games and then the World Championships, China's women's team has retained the same lineup.
With five regulars and one reserve, Du Siyu, Ke Qinqin, Zhang Qingying, Qiu Qiyuan, Zhang Yihan and Qin Xinyi, the team has claimed three consecutive team titles.
Chang likened the three competitions to "a small exam, a midterm, and a final," noting that the team "performed better with each successive event".
Captain Qiu said that with the same lineup competing together for the third time this year, the gymnasts had developed a clear understanding of how to arrange their routines.
"Go out there and execute your movements with confidence - just deliver a clean, polished routine, and that'll be enough."
A broader shift in training has also strengthened the team's overall performance. For years, the Chinese women's team has been particularly competitive on uneven bars and balance beam, while vault and floor exercise have often been its weaker apparatus.
Entering the Los Angeles Olympic cycle, the team has devoted greater attention to improving those weaker events.
Chang described the gymnastics team event as a "systematic battle".
That battle is still going on. ■

China issues stamps to mark 90th anniversary of Long March victory
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
15:25:16 CST
16:25:16 KST

BEIJING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- China Post on Thursday issued a set of six commemorative stamps marking the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, an epic undertaking in modern Chinese history.
These six stamps feature the following themes: the departure of the Red Army, the bloody Battle of the Xiangjiang River, the landmark Zunyi Meeting, the battle at Lazikou Pass, the victorious reunion of Red Army forces, and carrying forward the great Long March spirit.
In October 1934, the Communist Party of China (CPC) was forced to retreat from the Central Soviet Area in east China's Jiangxi Province and move northwest after enduring a series of encirclement campaigns by rival forces of the Chinese Kuomintang party.
The CPC-led Red Army broke through enemy blockades, crossed rugged terrain, and endured fierce battles and immense hardship. Tens of thousands of soldiers lost their lives along the way.
In the winter of 1934 during the Long March, the Red Army fought its way across the Xiangjiang River in Guangxi and broke through the Kuomintang troops' blockade, but suffered tens of thousands of casualties in the battle.
The Zunyi Meeting took place in January 1935. The meeting was a landmark event in the history of the CPC as it largely determined the fate of the Party at a critical juncture for its survival. In September that year, the Red Army captured Lazikou Pass, a narrow mountain pass flanked by steep cliffs in northwest China's Gansu Province, opening a route north. In October 1936, three main Red Army forces converged in northwestern China, marking the end of the Long March.
The Long March is never a story told merely within China. In his book "Red Star Over China," published in 1937, American journalist Edgar Snow introduced the Chinese revolution to international readers. Decades later, American journalist Harrison Salisbury retraced the route and described the Long March as "a great human epic."
The six-stamp set has a combined face value of 7.8 yuan (about 1.2 U.S. dollars), with 4.3 million sets planned for issuance. The stamps will be available for six months via designated postal outlets across China and online sales channels. ■

====================================================================================================

Profile: Where courage ends, skill begins -- the making of a rope rescuer
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
15:25:15 CST
16:25:15 KST

Jiang Shengqiang works at the crash site of the China Eastern Airlines flight MU5735 in Tengxian County, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, March 25, 2022. (Xinhua)
NANNING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- Deep inside an S-shaped cave in Liuzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Jiang Shengqiang and his team crawled through a passage barely wide enough for a single person.
Some 80 meters underground, a caver with multiple fractures could no longer move. Rescuers drilled through rock to open a route, fixed ropes at several points and placed firefighting jackets beneath the injured man to protect him from the jagged ground as they moved him toward the entrance.
Fifteen hours after the rescue began in February 2025, the man was brought safely to the surface.
For Jiang, captain of a mountain rescue team with the Liuzhou fire and rescue authority, the operation drew on skills he had spent years learning. His pursuit of those skills began with a rescue in 2008.
That year, Jiang and his colleagues were called after a young girl fell from a mountain and became caught in a tree more than 80 meters above the foot of the slope.
Specialized mountain rescue techniques were still largely unfamiliar to the team. The firefighters eventually reached the girl and brought her down, but the process took 10 hours.
"I saw how anxious her parents were, and I felt guilty," Jiang recalled. "Back then, courage was almost all we had. I knew we needed the skills to match."
His first systematic training came in 2016, when he attended a course on water and mountain rescue and was introduced to professional rope techniques.
He dedicated himself to mastering these skills.
With specialized equipment still scarce in his unit, Jiang spent more than 20,000 yuan (about 2,976 U.S. dollars) of his own savings on harnesses, fall-arrest devices and helmets. He bought manuals, studied training videos frame by frame and traveled to courses elsewhere in China whenever he had the chance.
Over the years, thousands of meters of rope were worn out in training. Within little more than two years, Jiang had mastered single- and double-rope techniques. By 2019, he was teaching other rescuers.
The work was also changing around him.
After China's fire and rescue forces were reorganized in 2018, their duties expanded beyond traditional firefighting to a broader range of emergencies. As of July 2021, China had established 179 specialized mountain rescue teams with more than 3,500 personnel, including 752 rescuers qualified in rope rescue, according to the Ministry of Emergency Management.
A national plan for fire and rescue work issued in 2022 called for stronger specialist teams for earthquakes, water and mountain rescue, among other fields.
Guangxi's extensive karst terrain presents particular challenges for rescuers, with steep mountains, caves, sinkholes and underground rivers common across the region. In some cases, difficult terrain and narrow passages make reaching an injured or trapped person a major part of the rescue itself.
In Liuzhou, Jiang began passing on what he had learned.
In 2024, a dedicated rope rescue training unit bearing Jiang's name was established. The training base where he works also became one of three in China's fire and rescue system certified by the Industrial Rope Access Trade Association, a British-based organization that sets training and technical standards for industrial rope access.
Jiang has trained all 20 members of his team. The team has developed more than 10 rescue procedures and modified a system used to reach people stranded by floodwaters, cutting the number of operators required from eight to five. Five of Jiang's proposals were later incorporated into a national rescue training syllabus.
These techniques have been tested far beyond the training grounds.
After the crash of China Eastern Airlines flight MU5735 in Guangxi in March 2022, Jiang joined the emergency response in Tengxian County. A seven-meter-long section of a wing weighing about 500 kilograms was lodged on a steep, muddy slope and needed to be moved without being deformed.
Jiang and his colleagues built a rope-based lowering system. With little firm footing on the slope, they cleared soil, secured the wreckage and lowered it to an evidence collection area. The operation took four hours.
In August this year, Jiang was working in a very different setting.
Heavy rain had flooded many parts of Ningming County in Guangxi, cutting off villages along the Mingjiang River. Jiang led an advance team across more than 30 kilometers of flooded terrain, at times wading through waist-deep water, to assess conditions and relay information from isolated communities.
He later joined crews evacuating residents by inflatable boat through flooded streets.
During one trip, an elderly resident frightened by the water gripped Jiang's arm.
"It's all right. We're firefighters," Jiang said. "Our boat is safe."
Over 19 years in the fire and rescue service, Jiang has taken part in more than 4,000 emergency operations and helped rescue more than 300 people.
At the mountain rescue training ground in Liuzhou, Jiang still carries a descender that has been with him for six years and used more than 1,000 times. Its metal surface has been rubbed bright.
"We do rescue work," Jiang said. "The better we master our skills, the more we live up to the profession." ■
Members of a mountain rescue team with the Liuzhou fire and rescue authority conducts rescue at a cave in Liuzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Feb. 8, 2025. (Xinhua)
Jiang Shengqiang (4th L) reviews rescue cases with team members at a training base in Liuzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, June 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Yang Chi)
Jiang Shengqiang (C, back) guides team members in rope rescue training at a training base in Liuzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, June 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Yang Chi)

New Zealand cyber agency urges immediate patching against PHP vulnerabilities
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
15:25:13 CST
16:25:13 KST

WELLINGTON, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- New Zealand's National Cyber Security Center (NCSC) on Thursday urged organizations to immediately apply security patches against critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language widely used in websites and web services.
The vulnerabilities could allow attackers to take full control of a website, web server or web service, including defacing or taking down websites, the NCSC said in a statement.
A patch was released by the PHP Foundation, which is responsible for the programming language, at 3 a.m. local time on Thursday. The NCSC said the update would protect underlying systems that rely on the PHP programming language, but further updates from software and web service providers might be required.
Older, end-of-life versions of PHP would remain vulnerable unless organizations apply custom patches or receive updates through enterprise operating system vendors, it said.
The NCSC advised organizations and individuals to monitor official PHP guidance and apply security patches as they become available and actively monitor for exploitation. Patching the exposed services will not remove already exploited systems.
Organizations unable to patch immediately should consider disabling public-facing web services, while checking with third-party suppliers to determine whether their systems use PHP and need to address these vulnerabilities, the agency said. ■

Feature: Antonelli finds value in restraint as maiden F1 title beckons
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
15:25:07 CST
16:25:07 KST

by Michael Butterworth
BEIJING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- At Monza, Kimi Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to claim an extraordinary home victory. Two races later in Baku, the Italian deliberately eased off the pace and settled for fifth.
The contrasting performances revealed two sides of a driver whose growing maturity has helped put him on the brink of becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion.
Now, after successive podium finishes in Malaysia and Singapore, the 20-year-old Mercedes driver heads into this weekend's United States Grand Prix with his first mathematical chance of securing the title.
"I was aware I was probably at 85% of what I could have achieved in terms of performance," Antonelli told Xinhua and one other outlet ahead of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia earlier this month, reflecting on his cautious approach in Baku.
"But I wasn't mentally prepared to drive 100% in the race, to be fully on the limit."
While Antonelli has continued accumulating points, teammate and nearest championship rival George Russell has endured a miserable run of results.
The Briton retired with engine failure in Malaysia, crashed out while leading the Singapore sprint, and finished only ninth in the main race after starting from the back of the grid following an engine change.
Antonelli, meanwhile, finished second in Malaysia and third in Singapore, having also taken fourth in the sprint.
The results have further strengthened his championship advantage and underlined the importance of consistency in a title fight, particularly for a driver whose natural instinct is to attack.
FROM ROOKIE STRUGGLES TO MONZA GLORY
Antonelli's recent performances also represent a remarkable turnaround from a year ago, when he was struggling to justify the faith Mercedes had placed in him.
Fast-tracked into Formula 1 at just 18 years old, Antonelli had been handed one of the sport's most coveted seats following seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton's surprise decision to leave Mercedes for Ferrari.
Having bypassed Formula 3 and completed only one season in Formula 2, the Italian arrived with considerable expectations but relatively little experience.
His rookie campaign proved inconsistent. Although he showed flashes of the talent that had persuaded Mercedes to promote him, Antonelli endured a difficult mid-season spell and was comprehensively outscored by Russell over the season.
Questions were raised about whether Mercedes had promoted him too early, and the pressure was particularly evident at Monza, where Antonelli spun into the gravel during practice before finishing a scrappy race in ninth place.
Even Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff, one of his staunchest supporters, described the performance as "underwhelming," although he maintained his confidence in the youngster's long-term potential.
Antonelli's response in 2026 has been emphatic. He claimed his maiden Formula 1 victory at round two in China Grand Prix, before winning the next four races to establish a commanding lead in the standings.
By the time he triumphed at August's Spanish Grand Prix, the Italian had taken his victory tally to eight, transforming himself from a promising but inconsistent rookie into the driver everyone else was chasing.
His transformation was perhaps most vividly illustrated at Monza. Twelve months after struggling so publicly at his home circuit, Antonelli charged through the field to claim one of the season's most remarkable victories.
"Monza so far is the most special win that I've ever had," Antonelli recalled. "I would have never thought to win the race from where I was starting."
The podium celebrations were almost as memorable as the drive itself.
"Hearing everyone singing the Italian anthem was very special and very emotional," he said.
"I actually didn't want to leave the podium in the moment."
LEARNING WHEN TO HOLD BACK
But if Monza demonstrated the rewards of relentless attacking, Baku offered a lesson in the value of restraint.
A disrupted practice program and a qualifying crash had left Antonelli towards the rear of the grid and shorn of confidence. Despite knowing that both he and his car were capable of more, he made a conscious decision not to push to the limit.
Antonelli acknowledged that he would have taken a "much more attacking" approach had the Azerbaijan Grand Prix occurred earlier in the season, when the championship picture was less clearly defined.
Instead, with an 81-point advantage at the time, he opted to bring the car home and secure valuable points, even as Russell stormed to victory.
"It was a decision that I took after the race start to say, 'I'm just going to try to bring it home, stay out of trouble, and then we'll see what the result is going to be.'"
It was the first time this season that Antonelli said he had deliberately chosen to drive within himself.
That decision did not come easily. He admitted feeling frustrated by his performance, particularly after the confidence-sapping mistake in qualifying.
But he also recognised that championships are not won solely through spectacular victories.
"Baku was one of those weekends where you have to be happy with fifth or this kind of result because obviously it's not the result you want, but still valuable points that can make a big impact at the end of the season."
That assessment has acquired greater significance following the races in Malaysia and Singapore, where Antonelli's consistent points-scoring contrasted sharply with Russell's setbacks.
Yet the Italian insists that his willingness to exercise caution when necessary should not be mistaken for a fundamental change in approach.
"I think what would help me is just thinking about going out there and trying to win every race," he said.
"Try to do my best and keep the focus, staying present on what I have to do in the moment, and then we'll see at the end of the year."
THE JOB IS NOT FINISHED
With the championship drawing closer, however, Antonelli acknowledged that shutting out thoughts of the title altogether was impossible.
"I've thought about [winning the title]," he said. "I constantly try to remind myself that it's not over until it's over."
For inspiration, Antonelli turned to a video of the late basketball legend Kobe Bryant during the 2009 NBA Finals.
Despite his Los Angeles Lakers holding a 2-0 lead over the Orlando Magic, Bryant remained unsmiling, insisting that the job was not yet finished.
"That was what I needed to see because it's true," Antonelli said.
"At the end of the day, I haven't achieved that yet. And it's not that because I have a big lead, I'm the one who can lose it because, at the end, you can't lose something that you haven't achieved yet.
"The only thing I can do is win it."
Antonelli's rapid rise has also brought new pressures away from the circuit, with his growing fame making it increasingly difficult to enjoy ordinary activities without attracting attention.
"You've also got to protect yourself," he said, explaining that the demands of public life could drain his energy and affect his concentration.
"If you don't protect yourself, then you can enter into this loop where you're down in energy and maybe lose a little bit of focus as well on the goal."
For now, however, his focus remains firmly on the immediate challenge.
Antonelli has no intention of simply nursing his championship advantage to the end of the season, believing that continuing to attack offers the best opportunity to settle the title battle as quickly as possible.
"The sooner it's finished, the better it is," he said. "The sooner it's finished, the less I need to worry about it later."
With Russell running out of opportunities to close the gap, Antonelli arrives at the Circuit of the Americas knowing that he could leave Texas as world champion.
Whether that happens this weekend or, as is more likely, later in the season, his contrasting performances at Monza and Baku illustrate the balance he has learned to strike.
For a driver approaching the biggest achievement of his career, knowing when to attack and when to hold back may prove the most important lesson of all. ■

China-Europe freight train service tops 140,000 trips
China

2026-10-22

A freight train loaded with containers departs from Puhe station in Shenyang, northeast China's Liaoning Province, Oct. 22, 2026. A China-Europe freight train bound for Moscow departed Puhe station in Shenyang, northeast China's Liaoning Province, at around 11:30 a.m. Thursday, bringing the service's cumulative trips to top 140,000 and transporting goods worth over 560 billion U.S. dollars since 2011. Within China, 96 scheduled routes for trains traveling at 120 km per hour link 132 cities along the western, central and eastern corridors, while overseas the network now runs on three lines: northern, central and southern. Together they reach 237 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 12 Asian countries, covering most parts of Eurasia, according to China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway), the national rail operator. The southern route is now operating on regular basis, running 746 trains in the first nine months of 2026, up 125 percent year on year. (Xinhua/Pan Yulong)
SHENYANG, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- A China-Europe freight train bound for Moscow departed Puhe station in Shenyang, northeast China's Liaoning Province, at around 11:30 a.m. Thursday, bringing the service's cumulative trips to top 140,000 and transporting goods worth over 560 billion U.S. dollars since 2011.
The milestone comes a decade after the service adopted the unified brand of China Railway Express in June 2016.
Annual trips rose from 1,702 in 2016 to 20,022 in 2025, an average annual increase of more than 30 percent, according to the National Development and Reform Commission. A single month's volume now equals the whole of 2016.
As a flagship project and a landmark brand of the Belt and Road Initiative, the China-Europe freight train service, also referred to as the "steel camel caravans," has established a comprehensive logistics network across Eurasia.
Within China, 96 scheduled routes for trains traveling at 120 km per hour link 132 cities along the western, central and eastern corridors, while overseas the network now runs on three lines: northern, central and southern. Together they reach 237 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 12 Asian countries, covering most parts of Eurasia, according to China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway), the national rail operator.
The southern route is now operating on regular basis, running 746 trains in the first nine months of 2026, up 125 percent year on year.
In May, the service set a monthly record of 1,965 trains and 197,000 TEUs.
An official with the logistics center of China Railway said the operator has been advancing infrastructure connectivity and the alignment of standards and rules to build a smooth, efficient, multi-directional network that links rails with sea routes. ■
